citations.narrative:
The facility failed to maintain complete and accurate inventory records. Incorrect numbers of wallabies, zebu, llamas,
sheep, goats, and cattle were listed as well as not listing the camel. Correct record keeping is necessary to properly
identify animals and to accurately trace animals to ensure their legal acquisition, health, and humane transportation.
Every dealer shall make, keep, and maintain records or forms which fully and correctly disclose acquisition and
disposition information regarding animals purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, leased, or otherwise in his or her
possession or under his or her control, or which is transported, sold, euthanized, or otherwise disposed of by that dealer.
Correct by: November 3, 2026.

The enclosure housing 10 sheep and 9 goats is not being maintained in good repair. There are multiple areas along the
bottom of the chain-link fencing that have come loose from the posts. In one area, the bottom of the fence has lifted into
the enclosure, and the wires have become loose. The animals could become entangled in the loose wires leading to
injury. Enclosures that are not kept in good repair can also result in escape. The facility must be constructed of such
material and of such strength as appropriate for the animals involved. Correct by making sure the housing facilities are
maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury and to contain the animals.
Correct by: November 10, 2026.

Four water receptacles had accumulated green-brown films throughout the bottom and sides. This includes a water tub
for 10 sheep and 9 goats, a water bucket for 2 coatimundis, a water tub for a camel, 2 alpacas, 4 llamas, 2 goats, 4
sheep, 2 water buffalo, 2 cows, and a zebu, and a water tub for a wallaby and 6 kangaroos. Unclean drinking water can
lead to contamination and disease, or dehydration if the animals are unwilling to drink it. Correct by ensuring all water
receptacles shall be kept clean and sanitary.
Correct by: November 3, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
